findings.title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a user-controlled negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django raises an AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') for negative slice bounds, so this produces a 500 error. Cursor.from_string accepts negative ints, so any admin sending optimized_pagination=true with a crafted cursor triggers it. The comment that the ORM handles negative slicing is wrong. The 'safe because permissions are checked' claim is also unfounded.

findings.title: BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` lets a negative offset reach queryset slicing whenever is_prev is true. Previously negative offsets failed in the same way, but this change deliberately keeps them for prev cursors, which affects every endpoint using BasePaginator. A crafted cursor such as `0:-5:1` would cause an assertion error and a 500 response. The change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.

findings.title: Unrelated feature gated on has_global_access, member may be None
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is dereferenced without a None check. A superuser who is not an org member has member=None, so evaluating the `or` right-hand side would raise AttributeError whenever is_superuser is False. Also, this audit-log pagination feature is unrelated to the spans buffer PR title, and it exposes the negative-offset path.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit reduced 10x
findings.body: The loop limit drops from 10000 to 1000 without explanation, and the comment explaining the limit was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 now fail to join correctly.

findings.title: Span count check removed; max_segment_spans is now unused
findings.body: The max_segment_spans check in _load_segment_data was removed and the Lua script now caps sets at 1000 via zpopmin. The cap is 1000 but max_segment_spans defaults to 1001, and the parameter is now dead code. Eviction also drops the lowest-scored (oldest end timestamp) spans silently, with no metric or log. The zpopmin only runs after the zunionstore merge, and spans zadd'd before the script (the pipeline step) can push the set well over the limit until later calls trim it.

findings.title: end_timestamp_precise accessed as required key
findings.body: val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError if a span lacks the field, which crashes the whole batch in the consumer. This is a poison-pill risk during rollout or for older Relay versions.
